questions.stem: This cross-section shows a thin-walled air sac with squamous lining cells, a scattered wandering phagocyte, a cuboidal cell secreting a thin film into the airspace, and a surrounding capillary containing red cells. Which cell type here is responsible for reducing surface tension and preventing collapse of this structure?

explanation.summary: The cuboidal type II pneumocyte secretes pulmonary surfactant, which lowers alveolar surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse at end-expiration. Type I pneumocytes form the thin gas-exchange surface, and macrophages clear debris; endothelial cells line the capillary.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cuboidal type II pneumocyte secretes pulmonary surfactant, which lowers alveolar surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse at end-expiration. Type I pneumocytes form the thin gas-exchange surface, and macrophages clear debris; endothelial cells line the capillary.

questions.stem: This H&E-stained section shows thin-walled air sacs opening off a larger conducting passage. From which organ is this tissue taken?

explanation.summary: The delicate polygonal air spaces (alveoli) with thin capillary-containing septa opening off a bronchiolar lumen are the defining histologic architecture of lung parenchyma, specialized for gas exchange.
explanation.whyCorrect: The delicate polygonal air spaces (alveoli) with thin capillary-containing septa opening off a bronchiolar lumen are the defining histologic architecture of lung parenchyma, specialized for gas exchange.

questions.stem: In this magnified developing lung, the airway is still lined by tall cuboidal cells with only sparse nearby capillaries. Which stage of lung development does this represent?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Terminal air sac stage with surfactant

explanation.summary: A thick cuboidal epithelium separated from capillaries by abundant mesoderm indicates an immature stage with a thick air-blood barrier; the epithelium has not yet thinned into type 1 pneumocytes needed for efficient gas exchange.
explanation.whyCorrect: A thick cuboidal epithelium separated from capillaries by abundant mesoderm indicates an immature stage with a thick air-blood barrier; the epithelium has not yet thinned into type 1 pneumocytes needed for efficient gas exchange.

questions.stem: This magnified alveolar wall shows flat cells lining most of the surface and scattered rounded granular cells at the corners, adjacent to capillaries. What is the key function of the rounded granular cell type shown?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formation of the thin gas-diffusion surface

choices.label: E
choices.text: Conduction of air to the alveoli

explanation.summary: The cuboidal granular cells are type 2 pneumocytes, which secrete surfactant that lowers surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse; the flat cells are type 1 pneumocytes forming the diffusion barrier.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cuboidal granular cells are type 2 pneumocytes, which secrete surfactant that lowers surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse; the flat cells are type 1 pneumocytes forming the diffusion barrier.

questions.stem: This timeline maps lung development onto gestational weeks. At approximately which point does the lung first become capable of supporting respiration (gas exchange)?

explanation.summary: Respiration becomes possible near the canalicular-to-saccular transition (~24-26 weeks) once a thin air-blood barrier forms and type 2 pneumocytes begin surfactant production, which is why this marks the threshold of viability for premature infants.
explanation.whyCorrect: Respiration becomes possible near the canalicular-to-saccular transition (~24-26 weeks) once a thin air-blood barrier forms and type 2 pneumocytes begin surfactant production, which is why this marks the threshold of viability for premature infants.

questions.stem: This sequence shows the foregut giving rise to a ventral outgrowth that is progressively partitioned. What process is being illustrated?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Formation of the diaphragm from the septum transversum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fusion of the pleural and pericardial cavities

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rotation of the primitive heart tube

choices.label: E
choices.text: Separation of the trachea from the esophagus

explanation.summary: The respiratory diverticulum buds from the ventral foregut and is separated from the future esophagus by tracheoesophageal ridges that fuse into a septum; failure of this process produces tracheoesophageal fistula.
explanation.whyCorrect: The respiratory diverticulum buds from the ventral foregut and is separated from the future esophagus by tracheoesophageal ridges that fuse into a septum; failure of this process produces tracheoesophageal fistula.

questions.stem: From 28 to 56 days, the paired outgrowths shown undergo repeated dichotomous division into progressively smaller branches. What does this branching establish?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The conducting airway tree and lung lobes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pulmonary venous return to the left atrium

explanation.summary: Sequential division of secondary and tertiary bronchial buds during the pseudoglandular period lays down the branching conducting airways and defines the lobar pattern (three lobes on the right, two on the left).
explanation.whyCorrect: Sequential division of secondary and tertiary bronchial buds during the pseudoglandular period lays down the branching conducting airways and defines the lobar pattern (three lobes on the right, two on the left).
